sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana kathyamānaṃ tvayā vipra rājñāṃ caritam uttamam
english: O ascetic wealth, O brahmin, I wish to hear in full detail, as narrated by you, the excellent conduct of kings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu viprendro dharmarājñā mahātmanā kathayām āsa māhātmyaṃ sagarasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the great-souled king of righteousness, that foremost of brahmins proceeded to narrate the greatness of the noble-souled Sagara.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ sagaro nāma pārthivaḥ rūpasattvabalopetaḥ sa cāputraḥ pratāpavān
english: Lomaśa said: Born in the lineage of the Ikṣvākus was a king named Sagara, endowed with beauty, virtue, and strength, yet childless and of great valour.

sanskrit: sa haihayān samutsādya tālajaṅghāṃś ca bhārata vaśe ca kṛtvā rājño 'nyān svarājyam anvaśāsata
english: Having destroyed the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas, O Bhārata, and having brought other kings under his sway, he ruled his own kingdom.

sanskrit: tasya bhārye tv abhavatāṃ rūpayauvanadarpite vaidarbhī bharataśreṣṭha śaibyā ca bharatarṣabha
english: He had two wives proud of their beauty and youth — the Vaidarbhī and the Śaibyā, O best of the Bhāratas, O bull among the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa putrakāmo nṛpatis tatāpa sumahat tapaḥ patnībhyāṃ saha rājendra kailāsaṃ girim āśritaḥ
english: That king, desiring sons, performed great austerities together with his two wives, O lord of kings, repairing to Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: sa tapyamānaḥ sumahat tapo yogasamanvitaḥ āsasāda mahātmānaṃ tryakṣaṃ tripuramardanam
english: While he was performing great austerities accompanied by the discipline of yoga, he approached the great-souled three-eyed one, the destroyer of Tripura.

sanskrit: śaṃkaraṃ bhavam īśānaṃ śūlapāniṃ pinākinam tryambakaṃ śivam ugreśaṃ bahurūpam umāpatim
english: Śaṅkara, Bhava, Īśāna, the trident-bearer, the wielder of the Pināka bow, Tryambaka, Śiva, the fierce lord, the many-formed, the husband of Umā.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvaiva varadaṃ patnībhyāṃ sahito nṛpaḥ praṇipatya mahābāhuḥ putrārthaṃ samayācata
english: Upon seeing that granter of boons, the king, together with his wives, prostrated himself — that mighty-armed one — and besought him for sons.

sanskrit: taṃ prītimān haraḥ prāha sabhāryaṃ nṛpasattamam yasmin vṛto muhūrte 'haṃ tvayeha nṛpate varam
english: Hara, greatly pleased, spoke to that best of kings along with his wife: 'In this very moment, O king, you have chosen me here for a boon.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi śūrāḥ samaradarpitāḥ ekasyāṃ saṃbhaviṣyanti patnyāṃ tava narottama
english: Sixty thousand heroic sons, proud in battle, shall be born from one of your wives, O best of men.

sanskrit: te caiva sarve sahitāḥ kṣayaṃ yāsyanti pārthiva eko vaṃśadharaḥ śūra ekasyāṃ saṃbhaviṣyati evam uktvā tu taṃ rudras tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Yet all of them together shall meet their destruction, O king; one heroic perpetuator of the lineage shall be born from the other wife.' Having said this to him, Rudra vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: sa cāpi sagaro rājā jagāma svaṃ niveśanam patnībhyāṃ sahitas tāta so 'tihṛṣṭamanās tadā
english: And King Sagara too returned to his own dwelling with his two wives, O dear one, his mind exceedingly joyful at that time.

sanskrit: tasyātha manujaśreṣṭha te bhārye kamalekṣaṇe vaidarbhī caiva śaibyā ca garbhiṇyau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
english: Then, O best of men, those two lotus-eyed wives of his — both the Vaidarbhī and the Śaibyā — became pregnant.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena vaidarbhī garbhālābuṃ vyajāyata śaibyā ca suṣuve putraṃ kumāraṃ devarūpiṇam
english: In the course of time the Vaidarbhī gave birth to a gourd of a womb, and Śaibyā gave birth to a son, a prince of divine appearance.

sanskrit: tadālābuṃ samutsraṣṭuṃ manaś cakre sa pārthivaḥ athāntarikṣāc chuśrāva vācaṃ gambhīranisvanām
english: The king resolved to cast away that gourd, but then from the sky he heard a voice of deep resonance.

sanskrit: rājan mā sāhasaṃ kārṣīḥ putrān na tyaktum arhasi alābumadhyān niṣkṛṣya bījaṃ yatnena gopyatām
english: 'O king, do not commit this rash act; you must not abandon your sons. Extract the seeds from within the gourd and preserve them with care.

sanskrit: sopasvedeṣu pātreṣu ghṛtapūrṇeṣu bhāgaśaḥ tataḥ putrasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭiṃ prāpsyasi pārthiva
english: Place them each in vessels filled with clarified butter and kept warm; then, O king, you shall obtain sixty thousand sons.

sanskrit: mahādevena diṣṭaṃ te putrajanma narādhipa anena kramayogena mā te buddhir ato 'nyathā
english: The birth of sons has been ordained for you by Mahādeva, O lord of men, through this graduated process — let your mind not think otherwise than this.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca etac chrutvāntarikṣāc ca sa rājā rājasattama yathoktaṃ tac cakārātha śraddadhad bharatarṣabha
english: Lomaśa said: Hearing this from the sky, that best of kings, O bull among the Bhāratas, did exactly as had been said, with faith.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi tasyāpratimatejasaḥ rudraprasādād rājarṣeḥ samajāyanta pārthiva
english: Sixty thousand sons of that royal sage of incomparable energy were born, O king, by the grace of Rudra.

sanskrit: te ghorāḥ krūrakarmāṇa ākāśaparisarpiṇaḥ bahutvāc cāvajānantaḥ sarvāṃl lokān sahāmarān
english: They were terrible, cruel in their deeds, roaming through the skies, and by reason of their great numbers they scorned all the worlds together with the gods.

sanskrit: tridaśāṃś cāpy abādhanta tathā gandharvarākṣasān sarvāṇi caiva bhūtāni śūrāḥ samaraśālinaḥ
english: They harassed the thirty gods as well as gandharvas and rakshasas, and all beings — those heroes distinguished in battle.

sanskrit: vadhyamānās tato lokāḥ sāgarair mandabuddhibhiḥ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ sahitāḥ sarvadaivataiḥ
english: The worlds, being tormented by those dull-witted Sagaras, took refuge with Brahmā, all the gods going together.

sanskrit: tān uvāca mahābhāgaḥ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ gacchadhvaṃ tridaśāḥ sarve lokaiḥ sārdhaṃ yathāgatam
english: The greatly blessed grandfather of all the worlds spoke to them: 'Go, all you thirty gods, along with the worlds, as you came.'

sanskrit: nātidīrgheṇa kālena sāgarāṇāṃ kṣayo mahān bhaviṣyati mahāghoraḥ svakṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ surāḥ
english: 'Within no very long time, O gods, there shall be a great and utterly terrible destruction of the Sagaras by their own deeds.'

sanskrit: evam uktās tato devā lokāś ca manujeśvara pitāmaham anujñāpya viprajagmur yathāgatam
english: Thus addressed, the gods and worlds, O lord of men, took leave of the Grandfather and dispersed as they had come.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāle bahutithe vyatīte bharatarṣabha dīkṣitaḥ sagaro rājā hayamedhena vīryavān tasyāśvo vyacarad bhūmiṃ putraiḥ suparirakṣitaḥ
english: Then, after much time had elapsed, O bull among the Bhāratas, the mighty King Sagara was initiated for the horse sacrifice, and his sacrificial horse roamed the earth well-guarded by his sons.

sanskrit: samudraṃ sa samāsādya nistoyaṃ bhīmadarśanam rakṣyamāṇaḥ prayatnena tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Reaching the ocean — waterless and terrible to behold — while being carefully guarded, it disappeared right there.

sanskrit: tatas te sāgarās tāta hṛtaṃ matvā hayottamam āgamya pitur ācakhyur adṛśyaṃ turagaṃ hṛtam tenoktā dikṣu sarvāsu sarve mārgata vājinam
english: Then those Sagaras, O dear one, thinking the best of horses had been stolen, came and reported to their father that the horse had been taken and was unseen; told by him they all searched for the steed in all directions.

sanskrit: tatas te pitur ājñāya dikṣu sarvāsu taṃ hayam amārganta mahārāja sarvaṃ ca pṛthivītalam
english: Then those Sagaras, by their father's command, searched for that horse in all directions, O great king, and all over the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tatas te sāgarāḥ sarve samupetya parasparam nādhyagacchanta turagam aśvahartāram eva ca
english: Then all those Sagaras, meeting together, could find neither the horse nor the horse-thief.

sanskrit: āgamya pitaraṃ cocus tataḥ prāñjalayo 'grataḥ sasamudravanadvīpā sanadīnadakandarā saparvatavanoddeśā nikhilena mahī nṛpa
english: Coming before their father with folded hands they reported: 'The entire earth with its oceans, forests, and islands, with its rivers, streams, and gorges, with its mountains, woodlands, and all its regions, O king —

sanskrit: asmābhir vicitā rājañ śāsanāt tava pārthiva na cāśvam adhigacchāmo nāśvahartāram eva ca
english: — has been searched by us, O king, by your command, O earth-lord; yet we find neither the horse nor the horse-thief.'

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ sa rājā krodhamūrchitaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ sarvāṃs tadā daivavaśān nṛpa
english: Hearing their words, that king, overcome with rage, spoke then to all of them — those who were subject to fate — O king.

sanskrit: anāgamāya gacchadhvaṃ bhūyo mārgata vājinam yajñiyaṃ taṃ vinā hy aśvaṃ nāgantavyaṃ hi putrakāḥ
english: 'Go and do not return; search again for the sacrificial steed. Without that horse you must not come back, O my sons.'

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu saṃdeśaṃ tatas te sagarātmajāḥ bhūya eva mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vicetum upacakramuḥ
english: Accepting that command, the sons of Sagara proceeded once again to search the entire earth.

sanskrit: athāpaśyanta te vīrāḥ pṛthivīm avadāritām samāsādya bilaṃ tac ca khanantaḥ sagarātmajāḥ kuddālair hreṣukaiś caiva samudram akhanaṃs tadā
english: Then those heroes saw the earth torn asunder; approaching that cavity, the sons of Sagara began digging it with mattocks and spades, and dug out the ocean at that time.

sanskrit: sa khanyamānaḥ sahitaiḥ sāgarair varuṇālayaḥ agacchat paramām ārtiṃ dāryamāṇaḥ samantataḥ
english: That abode of Varuṇa, being dug by the Sagaras together, suffered extreme distress as it was split on all sides.

sanskrit: asuroragarakṣāṃsi sattvāni vividhāni ca ārtanādam akurvanta vadhyamānāni sāgaraiḥ
english: Asuras, serpents, rakshasas, and various other creatures raised cries of anguish as they were slain by the Sagaras.

sanskrit: chinnaśīrṣā videhāś ca bhinnajānvasthimastakāḥ prāṇinaḥ samadṛśyanta śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Creatures with severed heads, dismembered, with broken knees, bones, and skulls were seen by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi khanatāṃ teṣāṃ samudraṃ makarālayam vyatītaḥ sumahān kālo na cāśvaḥ samadṛśyata
english: As they dug in this way through the ocean, the abode of the makaras, a very great time passed, yet the horse was not seen.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvottare deśe samudrasya mahīpate vidārya pātālam atha saṃkruddhāḥ sagarātmajāḥ apaśyanta hayaṃ tatra vicarantaṃ mahītale
english: Then in the northeastern region of the ocean, O lord of the earth, the enraged sons of Sagara, having rent open the underworld, saw the horse roaming there on the ground.

sanskrit: kapilaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ tejorāśim anuttamam tapasā dīpyamānaṃ taṃ jvālābhir iva pāvakam
english: And they saw the great-souled Kapila, that unsurpassed mass of energy, blazing with austerity like fire with its flames.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca te taṃ dṛṣṭvā hayaṃ rājan saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhāḥ anādṛtya mahātmānaṃ kapilaṃ kālacoditāḥ saṃkruddhāḥ samadhāvanta aśvagrahaṇakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Seeing that horse, O king, their hair bristling with excitement, disregarding the great-souled Kapila, driven by fate, they rushed forward in fury, eager to seize the horse.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja kapilo munisattamaḥ vāsudeveti yaṃ prāhuḥ kapilaṃ munisattamam
english: Then Kapila, that best of sages, became enraged, O great king — that best of sages whom they call Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: sa cakṣur vivṛtaṃ kṛtvā tejas teṣu samutsṛjan dadāha sumahātejā mandabuddhīn sa sāgarān
english: He, of surpassing energy, opened his eyes and releasing his fiery power upon them, burned those dull-witted Sagaras.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā bhasmasād bhūtān nāradaḥ sumahātapāḥ sagarāntikam āgacchat tac ca tasmai nyavedayat
english: Seeing them reduced to ashes, Nārada of very great austerity came to Sagara and reported this to him.

sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā vaco ghoraṃ rājā munimukhodgatam muhūrtaṃ vimanā bhūtvā sthāṇor vākyam acintayat ātmānam ātmanāśvāsya hayam evānvacintayat
english: Hearing that terrible word issued from the mouth of the sage, the king became dejected for a moment, then contemplated the words of the Immovable One; consoling himself, he then reflected only on the horse.

sanskrit: aṃśumantaṃ samāhūya asamajñaḥsutaṃ tadā pautraṃ bharataśārdūla idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Summoning Aṃśumat, the son of Asamañjas, his grandson, O tiger among the Bhāratas, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭis tāni sahasrāṇi putrāṇām amitaujasām kāpilaṃ teja āsādya matkṛte nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: 'Sixty thousand sons of mine of immeasurable energy have met their death on my account, having encountered the fiery power of Kapila.

sanskrit: tava cāpi pitā tāta parityakto mayānagha dharmaṃ saṃrakṣamāṇena paurāṇāṃ hitam icchatā
english: And your father too, O dear blameless one, was abandoned by me while I was protecting righteousness and seeking the welfare of the townspeople.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kimarthaṃ rājaśārdūlaḥ sagaraḥ putram ātmajam tyaktavān dustyajaṃ vīraṃ tan me brūhi tapodhana
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For what reason did King Sagara, that tiger among kings, abandon his own son, that hero so hard to abandon? Tell me this, O wealth of austerity.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca asamañjā iti khyātaḥ sagarasya suto hy abhūt yaṃ śaibyā janayām āsa paurāṇāṃ sa hi dārakān khureṣu krośato gṛhya nadyāṃ cikṣepa durbalān
english: Lomaśa said: There was a son of Sagara known as Asamañjas, whom Śaibyā bore — he would seize the children of the townspeople who were crying, and fling the helpless little ones into the river.

sanskrit: tataḥ paurāḥ samājagmur bhayaśokapariplutāḥ sagaraṃ cābhyayācanta sarve prāñjalayaḥ sthitāḥ
english: Then the townspeople came together, overwhelmed with fear and grief, and all of them besought Sagara, standing with folded hands.

sanskrit: tvaṃ nas trātā mahārāja paracakrādibhir bhayaiḥ asamañjobhayād ghorāt tato nas trātum arhasi
english: 'You are our protector, O great king, from fears such as enemy armies; from this terrible fear of Asamañjas you must therefore protect us.'

sanskrit: paurāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā ghoraṃ nṛpatisattamaḥ muhūrtaṃ vimanā bhūtvā sacivān idam abravīt
english: Hearing that terrible word of the townspeople, that best of kings became dejected for a moment and then spoke thus to his ministers.

sanskrit: asamañjāḥ purād adya suto me vipravāsyatām yadi vo matpriyaṃ kāryam etac chīghraṃ vidhīyatām
english: 'My son Asamañjas is to be expelled from the city today. If you wish to do what is pleasing to me, let this be done swiftly.'

sanskrit: evam uktā narendreṇa sacivās te narādhipa yathoktaṃ tvaritāś cakrur yathājñāpitavān nṛpaḥ
english: Thus addressed by that lord of men, those ministers, O lord of men, swiftly did exactly as had been said and as the king had commanded.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathā putro mahātmanā paurāṇāṃ hitakāmena sagareṇa vivāsitaḥ
english: All this has been narrated to you — how the son was exiled by the great-souled Sagara who desired the welfare of the townspeople.

sanskrit: aṃśumāṃs tu maheṣvāso yad uktaḥ sagareṇa ha tat te sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi kīrtyamānaṃ nibodha me
english: What was said to Aṃśumat, that great archer, by Sagara — all that I shall now tell you as it is recounted; hear it from me.

sanskrit: sagara uvāca pituś ca te 'haṃ tyāgena putrāṇāṃ nidhanena ca alābhena tathāśvasya paritapyāmi putraka
english: Sagara said: I am tormented, my child, by the abandonment of your father, and by the death of my sons, and likewise by the non-recovery of the horse.

sanskrit: tasmād duḥkhābhisaṃtaptaṃ yajñavighnāc ca mohitam hayasyānayanāt pautra narakān māṃ samuddhara
english: Therefore, from the hellish state in which I am, scorched by grief and deluded by this obstacle to the sacrifice — rescue me, O grandson, by bringing back the horse.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca aṃśumān evam uktas tu sagareṇa mahātmanā jagāma duḥkhāt taṃ deśaṃ yatra vai dāritā mahī
english: Lomaśa said: Thus addressed by the great-souled Sagara, Aṃśumat departed with a sorrowful heart toward the place where the earth had been split open.

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva mārgeṇa samudraṃ praviveśa ha apaśyac ca mahātmānaṃ kapilaṃ turagaṃ ca tam
english: He entered the ocean by that very same path and saw there the great-souled Kapila and that horse.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā tejaso rāśiṃ purāṇam ṛṣisattamam praṇamya śirasā bhūmau kāryam asmai nyavedayat
english: Seeing that ancient best of sages, that mass of radiance, he bowed his head to the ground in prostration and reported his purpose to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahātejāḥ kalipo 'ṃśumato 'bhavat uvāca cainaṃ dharmātmā varado 'smīti bhārata
english: Then the greatly radiant Kapila became pleased with Aṃśumat, and that righteous-souled one spoke to him saying 'I am a granter of boons,' O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa vavre turagaṃ tatra prathamaṃ yajñakāraṇāt dvitīyam udakaṃ vavre pitṝṇāṃ pāvanepsayā
english: He chose the horse as the first boon, for the sake of the sacrifice; the second boon he chose was water — desiring purification for the ancestral spirits.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejāḥ kapilo munipuṃgavaḥ dadāni tava bhadraṃ te yad yat prārthayase 'nagha
english: The greatly radiant Kapila, foremost of sages, spoke to him: 'I grant you whatever you seek, blessings be upon you, O blameless one.'

sanskrit: tvayi kṣamā ca dharmaś ca satyaṃ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam tvayā kṛtārthaḥ sagaraḥ putravāṃś ca tvayā pitā
english: 'Forbearance, righteousness, and truth are established in you. Sagara is fulfilled through you, and your father too has sons through you.

sanskrit: tava caiva prabhāvena svargaṃ yāsyanti sāgarāḥ pautraś ca te tripathagāṃ tridivād ānayiṣyati pāvanārthaṃ sāgarāṇāṃ toṣayitvā maheśvaram
english: 'By your very power shall the Sagaras ascend to heaven; and your grandson shall bring down the triple-pathed one from the celestial realm, having pleased Maheśvara, for the purpose of purifying the Sagaras.'

sanskrit: hayaṃ nayasva bhadraṃ te yajñiyaṃ narapuṃgava yajñaḥ samāpyatāṃ tāta sagarasya mahātmanaḥ
english: 'Take the sacrificial horse — blessings upon you, O bull among men; let the sacrifice of the great-souled Sagara be completed, O dear one.'

sanskrit: aṃśumān evam uktas tu kapilena mahātmanā ājagāma hayaṃ gṛhya yajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Kapila, Aṃśumat came back with the horse to the sacrificial enclosure of the great-souled king.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya tataḥ pādau sagarasya mahātmanaḥ mūrdhni tenāpy upāghrātas tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat
english: He then saluted the feet of the great-souled Sagara, was smelled on the head by him, and reported everything to him.

sanskrit: yathā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ cāpi sāgarāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ tathā taṃ cāsmai hayam ācaṣṭa yajñavāṭam upāgatam
english: He described to him the destruction of the Sagaras as he had seen and heard it, and told him of the horse that had come to the sacrificial enclosure.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā sagaro rājā putrajaṃ duḥkham atyajat aṃśumantaṃ ca saṃpūjya samāpayata taṃ kratum
english: Hearing this, King Sagara set aside the grief born of his sons' fate, honored Aṃśumat, and completed that sacrifice.

sanskrit: samāptayajñaḥ sagaro devaiḥ sarvaiḥ sabhājitaḥ putratve kalpayām āsa samudraṃ varuṇālayam
english: With his sacrifice completed, Sagara, honored by all the gods, declared the ocean — the abode of Varuṇa — to be his son.

sanskrit: praśāsya suciraṃ kālaṃ rājyaṃ rājīvalocanaḥ pautre bhāraṃ samāveśya jagāma tridivaṃ tadā
english: That lotus-eyed one, having ruled the kingdom for a very long time, placed the burden upon his grandson and departed to the three heavens.

sanskrit: aṃśumān api dharmātmā mahīṃ sāgaramekhalām praśaśāsa mahārāja yathaivāsya pitāmahaḥ
english: And Aṃśumat, righteous-souled, ruled the earth girt by the ocean, O great king, just as his grandfather had done.

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ samabhavad dilīpo nāma dharmavit tasmai rājyaṃ samādhāya aṃśumān api saṃsthitaḥ
english: His son was born — named Dilīpa, a knower of righteousness; having entrusted the kingdom to him, Aṃśumat too passed away.
